California sea lion fact: Ronan is the first nonhuman mammal proven to keep a precise beat to music.
She bobs her head in perfect sync, and recent studies say she often matches or beats human consistency.
She can do it with brand new rhythms she has never heard before, which is the part that rules out simple memorization.

#sealion #marinemammals #animalcognition #oceanlife
alt: A California sea lion resting on a rock with its head raised, whiskers and dark eyes visible.
comments: Beat-keeping was considered a vocal-learning trait, something only animals that learn sounds could do. Sea lions are not vocal learners, which is why Ronan mattered so much to the research.

posts.text:
Bearded dragon care costs: the dragon itself is the cheap part, and the setup is where the budget actually goes.
Husbandry standards have moved on from old care sheets. Bigger enclosures, stronger UVB, more careful temperature gradients.
Give a new dragon 7 to 14 days to settle before you pick it up.
The diet flips as it grows, from mostly bugs to mostly greens.
Most serious health problems trace back to husbandry, not bad luck, which means most of the list is preventable.

#beardeddragon #beardeddragoncare #reptilecare #petlizard
alt: Fully furnished bearded dragon enclosure with basking platform and UVB lighting
Bearded dragon basking under a UVB light in a fully equipped enclosure
Bearded dragon eating chopped leafy greens and a calcium-dusted cricket
Person gently holding a bearded dragon with a full underhand grip
Veterinarian examining a bearded dragon on an exam table
comments: The UVB bulb is the line item people skip and the one that causes metabolic bone disease. It also degrades on a schedule, so it needs replacing long before it stops visibly glowing.

Chicken fact: in 1945 a rooster called Miracle Mike lived over 18 months after his head was chopped off.
The axe missed his brain stem, which left enough function intact for him to keep going.
He became a traveling sideshow attraction on the strength of it.

#chickens #poultry #animalfacts #weirdhistory
alt: A brown and white rooster standing in grass with its comb and wattles clearly visible.
comments: The brain stem is what runs breathing and heart rate in birds, which is the whole reason the survival was possible rather than a hoax.

posts.text:
Wallace's flying frog does not just jump between trees, it glides and steers.
Enormous webbed feet work as parachutes and rudders at the same time.
That lets it control the descent and pick a landing branch instead of just falling with style.

#flyingfrog #amphibians #rainforest #wildlifefacts
alt: A green tree frog with oversized webbed feet gripping a branch, webbing visible between the toes.
comments: It is named for Alfred Russel Wallace, who worked out natural selection alongside Darwin and collected the first specimen in Borneo.

posts.text:
Tarantula care: they are one of the most affordable exotic pets to keep, upfront and over time.
The catch is that a female can live 15 to 20 years or more, so the low sticker price is misleading if you only look at year one.
Enclosures are refreshingly simple, no complex lighting, no elaborate gradients. Shape and substrate depth are what matter.
A tarantula refusing food for weeks is usually premolt, not a red flag.
Handling is the real risk. A fall from your hand can rupture the abdomen and that is often fatal.

#tarantula #tarantulakeeper #invertebrates #exoticpets
alt: Tarantula enclosure with substrate, cork bark hide, and water dish
Chilean rose hair tarantula beside its enclosure setup and feeding tongs
Tarantula feeding on a cricket inside its enclosure
Tarantula being gently guided with long tongs during enclosure maintenance
Tarantula near a shallow water dish showing healthy posture in its enclosure
comments: Veterinary care for tarantulas is genuinely limited, many areas have no vet who treats invertebrates at all, which is why correct husbandry does nearly all the work here.

posts.text:
Hairy frog fact: males grow temporary hair during breeding season, and it is not hair at all.
Those frills are skin packed with blood vessels, grown along the sides and legs.
They let the males absorb extra oxygen while guarding eggs in fast-flowing, low-oxygen streams.

#hairyfrog #amphibians #frogsofinstagram #wildlifefacts
alt: A hairy frog on wet rock, with fine hair-like fringes of skin visible along its sides and thighs.
comments: The hair only appears in breeding males and disappears afterward, which is why it took a while to be understood as a parenting adaptation rather than a permanent feature.

posts.text:
Penguin fact: male gentoo and Adelie penguins court by finding the smoothest pebble they can and presenting it.
If she accepts, the pebble goes into the nest they build together.
Those pairings often turn into a lifelong bond, which makes the pebble a genuinely high-stakes gift.

#penguins #gentoopenguin #antarctica #wildlifefacts
alt: Two penguins standing close together on rocky ground, one facing the other.
comments: Nest pebbles are scarce enough in a colony that penguins have been filmed stealing them from neighbors, which makes the smooth ones genuinely valuable currency.

posts.text:
Rabbit care costs more than the adoption fee suggests, once spay or neuter and years of vegetables are counted.
The small wire hutch sold as a rabbit cage is considered genuinely inadequate under current welfare standards.
A rabbit's gut depends on constant food throughput, so a skipped meal deserves same-day attention, not wait and see.
An unsupported rabbit can fracture its own lumbar spine struggling to get free.
They need a rabbit-savvy exotic vet, not a standard small-animal clinic, and finding one before you need one matters.

#rabbits #rabbitcare #bunnycare #housebunny
alt: Rabbit exercise pen setup with litter box, hay feeder, and hides
Rabbit in a fully equipped exercise pen with hay and dishes
Rabbit eating fresh hay and leafy greens
Rabbit being carried securely with full body support against a person
Rabbit being examined by an exotic veterinarian
comments: Finding the exotic vet before you need one is the part people skip. A rabbit in GI stasis is not the moment to start searching, and a standard small-animal clinic may not carry rabbit-safe protocols.

posts.text:
Woodpecker fact: they peck up to 20 times a second without concussions, and the shock-absorbing skull explanation is wrong.
A 2022 study debunked it. The skull actually stays rigid, which lets them hammer harder.
They avoid injury because the brain is tiny and each impact is too brief to do damage.

#woodpecker #birdfacts #ornithology #wildlifefacts
alt: A woodpecker clinging to a tree trunk mid-peck, head turned toward the bark.
comments: A cushioned skull would actually waste energy, since it would absorb force meant for the wood. Rigidity is the feature, not the flaw.

Ocean sunfish fact: a mola mola lays up to 300 million eggs at once, more than any other vertebrate on Earth.
Almost none of them survive to adulthood.
The entire strategy is volume, banking on sheer numbers rather than protecting any individual egg.

#oceansunfish #molamola #marinebiology #oceanfacts
alt: An ocean sunfish swimming near the surface, its tall flattened body and blunt tail visible.
comments: An adult mola can reach over 2,000 kg, which makes the size gap between the egg and the finished animal one of the largest of any vertebrate.

posts.text:
African grey parrot care is one of the most expensive commitments on this site, and the purchase price is only the entry fee.
The cage has to support a genuinely large, intelligent, long-lived bird, and placement matters as much as size.
This species is specifically prone to calcium deficiency in a way other large parrots are not, which makes diet more consequential here.
They need roughly 4 to 5 hours of daily interaction to stay well-adjusted.
They are also more prone to a few specific conditions than the smaller parrots we cover.

#africangreyparrot #africangrey #parrotcare #birdsofinstagram
alt: African grey parrot cage set up with appropriately sized bars, varied perches, and foraging toys
African grey parrot perched beside its cage and accessories, representing the total cost of ownership
African grey parrot eating formulated pellets and fresh vegetables
African grey parrot interacting closely with its owner, reflecting the daily time commitment this species needs
African grey parrot undergoing a vet exam to check for signs of illness
comments: The calcium vulnerability is the detail most new owners miss. It is why a seed-heavy diet does more damage in this species than it would in a comparable parrot of the same size.
